title: Halting During the Walk Phase
statement: Let $a,b,f,B$ be natural numbers, let $m$ be a Boolean, let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input symbols, and let $x$ and $\beta$ be Boolean strings. Suppose a state $st$ of fifteen natural-number registers has every register at most $B$, and its registers $d,u,t,c,z,n,m$ satisfy $st.d=st.u=st.t=st.c=st.z=0$, $st.n=2\cdot 2^{st.e}$, and $st.m=2(2^{st.e})^2$. The register program started on the pair encoding of $x$ and $\beta$, at the comparison instruction for the unary-block length, with registers given by $st$ and no answer yet, halts with the following answer, and every configuration before it halts satisfies the program’s instruction preconditions and has all registers at most $B$. If the mode is true, the answer is true exactly when $st.i<2(2^{st.e})^2+2\cdot2^{st.e}+7$. If the mode is false, the answer is true when $st.i<2\cdot2^{st.e}$, false when $st.i=2\cdot2^{st.e}$, true when $st.i=2\cdot2^{st.e}+1$, and otherwise is determined by the following rule: put $q=st.i-(2\cdot2^{st.e}+2)$; for $q<2(2^{st.e})^2$, it is the edge predicate for source $\lfloor q/2^{st.e}\rfloor$ and target $q\bmod 2^{st.e}$, using $N$, input $x$, and radius $st.s$; for larger $q$, it is the entry at offset $q-2(2^{st.e})^2$ in the string $(0,1,0,1,1)$, with out-of-range entries false. The edge predicate holds when the source is $0$ and the target encodes an initial configuration of $N$, when the target is $1$ and the source encodes an accepting configuration, or when both are at least $2$ and the corresponding configuration codes are related by one nondeterministic step; these encodings use input $x$ and radius $st.s$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input symbols
Every register of $st$ is at most $B$
replaced:
Let $a,b,f,B$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{mode}$ be a Boolean, let $N$ be a
finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over bits, and let $x,\beta$ be bit
strings. Suppose the register state $\mathrm{st}$ has all fifteen registers at most $B$,
and satisfies $\mathrm{st}.d=\mathrm{st}.u=\mathrm{st}.t=\mathrm{st}.c=\mathrm{st}.z=0$,
$\mathrm{st}.n=2\cdot 2^{\mathrm{st}.e}$, and $\mathrm{st}.m=2(2^{\mathrm{st}.e})^2$.
With the oracle determined by $N$, the program on the paired encoding of $x$ and
$\beta$, started in the walk phase with register values given by $\mathrm{st}$ and no
answer yet, halts with answer
$\mathrm{wAns}(N,x,\mathrm{mode},\mathrm{st}.s,\mathrm{st}.e,\mathrm{st}.i)$; every
configuration before halting satisfies the guard requiring the instruction's
precondition and all registers to be at most $B$.
